reason: The provided sources fully support a 45-second script about the sperm whale's record-breaking loudness and brain size, with numerous verified claims across multiple sites.
story: The sperm whale is a true record breaker of the deep ocean. It boasts the largest brain of any animal on Earth, weighing over fifteen pounds and growing more than five times heavier than a human brain. But its most astonishing superpower is sound. Using a massive head filled with waxy oil called spermaceti, the sperm whale generates clicks reaching an incredible 236 decibels underwater. This makes it officially the loudest animal on the planet. Researchers use these powerful echolocation clicks not only to hunt squid in pitch-black depths reaching over 7,000 feet, but also to calculate the exact size of each whale from miles away. Once hunted relentlessly for its valuable oil and ambergris, this ocean giant remains an enduring symbol of the mysteries of the deep.
angle: The sperm whale is the loudest animal on Earth, producing bone-rattling clicks at 236 decibels.

claims.claim: The sperm whale is the loudest animal on Earth.
Sperm whale vocalizations reach a source level of 236 decibels underwater.
The sperm whale has the largest brain of any known modern or extinct animal.
Sperm whales possess a waxy substance in their heads called spermaceti.
Sperm whales can dive to depths of 2,250 meters (7,380 feet).
The sperm whale has a single S-shaped blowhole situated asymmetrically on the left side of its head.
Female sperm whales form matriarchal social units while mature males often live solitary lives.
Sperm whale teeth are cone-shaped, weigh up to 1 kilogram each, and are located on the lower jaw.
The sperm whale is listed as endangered under the Endangered Species Act.
Commercial whaling from the 1800s to the 1980s severely reduced sperm whale populations.
The International Whaling Commission placed a moratorium on commercial whaling in 1986.

disputed: Historical claims of individual sperm whales exceeding 80 feet in length are considered exaggerations or measurement errors by some sources and should be attributed or handled carefully.
